description: @hawiyah/vanilla 0.3.0 creates the tab bar without the data-orientation attribute that the React, Vue and Angular adapters write; the appearance and the accessibility tree are the same. Removed when the guide pins a release that corrects createTabs.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: The vanilla Tabs controller (`createTabs`) creates the tab bar (`.hw-tab-bar`) without the `data-orientation` attribute

description: In 0.3.0 React and Vue write aria-labelledby on the input, Angular always writes data-size, data-variant and autocomplete, and Vue writes an empty value; no single vanilla markup equals the three. The accessibility tree and the rendering are compared in full. Removed when the guide pins a release in which the four results agree.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: TextField: React and Vue write `aria-labelledby` on the input next to the `for` of its label

description: @hawiyah/angular 0.3.0 always writes data-variant on the service card and always renders its icon region, which React, Vue and the vanilla markup write only when given. The accessibility tree and the rendering are compared in full. Removed when the guide pins a release that corrects hw-service-card.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: ServiceCard (Angular) always writes `data-variant` (`default` when no variant is given)

description: @hawiyah/vue 0.3.0 always writes data-collapse-at and data-side on Stack, which React writes only when the props are given and Angular and the vanilla markup never write on Stack. The accessibility tree and the rendering are compared in full. Removed when the guide pins a release that corrects the layout primitives of @hawiyah/vue.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: Stack (Vue), with the other layout primitives built by the same function,

description: In 0.3.0 React, Vue and Angular write max="100" on the progress element when max is not given, also on an indeterminate bar, where the vanilla markup writes no max; the appearance and the accessibility tree are the same. Only max on .hw-progress is left out of the comparison with the vanilla result, and the three framework results are compared with each other in full. Removed when the guide pins a release in which the four results agree.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: Progress (React, Vue, Angular) writes `max="100"` when `max` is not given, also on an indeterminate bar

description: In 0.3.0 React, Vue and Angular render the icon of IconButton inside a wrapper span[aria-hidden=true], where the vanilla markup of the @hawiyah/vanilla README puts aria-hidden on the span.hw-icon itself, and Angular also writes data-shape="square" and an empty value on the button (a second entry of the same Known defects list). A difference of the three framework results against the vanilla markup in an element cannot be ignored attribute by attribute, so the structure aspect is left out of the groups that name this entry; the accessibility tree and the rendering are compared in full. Removed when the guide pins a release in which the four results agree.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: IconButton (React, Vue, Angular) renders the icon inside a wrapper `span[aria-hidden="true"]`

description: In 0.3.0 a TextField inside Field renders differently in each adapter: in Angular hw-text-field nests its own div.hw-field inside hw-field and writes aria-labelledby, data-size, data-variant and autocomplete on its input, React and Vue write aria-labelledby on the input and Vue also an empty value; and Field does not track the value presence of a native control in React, Vue or Angular, so only the vanilla enhance() writes data-hw-filled on the .hw-input of the required and error groups. No single vanilla markup equals the three, and an attribute that the vanilla result writes cannot be ignored, so the structure aspect is left out of the groups that name this entry. The accessibility tree and the rendering are compared in full. Removed when the guide pins a release in which the four results agree.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: Field: in Angular a value control such as `hw-text-field` inside `hw-field` renders its own `div.hw-field` around its input

description: In 0.3.0 React and Vue write aria-labelledby on the textarea, Angular always writes data-size and data-variant, and Vue writes the value as a value attribute (empty when there is none) while Angular sets it as a property, so neither has the text content that the vanilla markup and React write for an initial value; no single vanilla markup equals the three. The accessibility tree and the rendering are compared in full. Removed when the guide pins a release in which the four results agree.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: Textarea: React and Vue write `aria-labelledby` on the textarea next to the `for` of its label

description: In 0.3.0 React and Vue write aria-labelledby on the input, Vue writes an empty value, and Angular writes hw-number-field on the div.hw-field wrapper instead of the input and always writes step; no single vanilla markup equals the three. The accessibility tree and the rendering are compared in full. Removed when the guide pins a release in which the four results agree.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: NumberField: React and Vue write `aria-labelledby` on the input next to the `for` of its label

description: In 0.3.0 Angular always writes data-size on .hw-input-group, which React, Vue and the vanilla markup write only when given, and React and Vue write no data-hw-filled on the native .hw-input of the group, which the vanilla enhance() and Angular write; the empty addon that Angular always renders is an entry of empty-elements.json. A difference in which Angular alone differs, or in which the vanilla result writes the attribute, cannot be ignored attribute by attribute, so the structure aspect is left out of the groups that name this entry. The accessibility tree and the rendering are compared in full. Removed when the guide pins a release in which the four results agree.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: InputGroup (Angular) always writes `data-size` (`md` when no size is given) on `.hw-input-group`

description: In 0.3.0 Vue writes an id on label.hw-choice, aria-labelledby, value="on" and data-hw-filled on the input, and Angular sets the checked state as a property, so a checked switch has no checked attribute there; the vanilla markup and React agree, and a difference of one adapter alone cannot be ignored attribute by attribute. The accessibility tree and the rendering are compared in full. Removed when the guide pins a release in which the four results agree.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: Switch (Vue) writes an `id` on `label.hw-choice`, `aria-labelledby` on the input pointing to that label

description: In 0.3.0 Vue writes an id on label.hw-choice, aria-labelledby, value="on" and data-hw-filled on the input, and Angular sets the checked state as a property, so a checked checkbox has no checked attribute there; the vanilla markup and React agree, and a difference of one adapter alone cannot be ignored attribute by attribute. The accessibility tree and the rendering are compared in full. Removed when the guide pins a release in which the four results agree.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: Checkbox (Vue) writes an `id` on `label.hw-choice`, `aria-labelledby` on the input pointing to that label

description: In 0.3.0 Vue writes an id on label.hw-choice, aria-labelledby and data-hw-filled on each input, and Angular hw-radio-group sets the checked state as a property, so the selected radio has no checked attribute there. React and Vue Radio are single options, each rendered in its own div.hw-field as their READMEs document, while the vanilla markup and Angular hw-radio-group place the label.hw-choice options directly in the fieldset; that wrapper element cannot be ignored attribute by attribute either, so the structure aspect is left out of the groups that name this entry. The accessibility tree and the rendering are compared in full. Removed when the guide pins a release in which the four results agree.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: Radio (Vue) writes an `id` on `label.hw-choice`, `aria-labelledby` on the input pointing to that label

description: In 0.3.0 React and Vue write aria-labelledby on the select, Vue writes a value attribute on a select that holds a value, and Angular always writes data-size and data-variant and selects the chosen option as a property, without a selected attribute; no single vanilla markup equals the three. The accessibility tree and the rendering are compared in full. Removed when the guide pins a release in which the four results agree.
source: CHANGELOG.md, 0.3.0, Known defects in 0.3.0: Select: React and Vue write `aria-labelledby` on the select next to the `for` of its label

description: In 0.3.0 React and Vue write aria-labelledby on the range input, Vue writes data-hw-filled, React writes readonly for readOnly, and Angular sets the value as a property, so its input has no value attribute; no single vanilla markup equals the three. The accessibility tree and the rendering are compared in full. Removed when the guide pins a release in which the four results agree.

description: In 0.3.0 React and Vue write aria-labelledby on the file input next to the for of its label, where the vanilla markup and Angular write none; the vanilla result agrees with Angular, so the attribute cannot be ignored in the comparison with it, and the structure aspect is left out of the groups that name this entry.
